mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates for equity valuation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of observations when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and SPX 20-day returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month, or the Rank IC between UNRATE change and SPX 5-day returns is below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer demand (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown that reduces corporate profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS and INDPRO both decline, or the Rank IC between the interaction term (RSAFS change * INDPRO change) and SPX 60-day returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a decline in CPIAUCSL below 2.0% annually signals disinflationary pressures that may prompt Fed easing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL < 2.0% annually, or the Rank IC between the interaction term and SPX 20-day returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of observations when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC between PAYEMS and SPX 5-day returns is below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 5% signals a contraction in the residential sector that reduces overall economic activity and corporate revenue, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST falls > 5% in 1 month, or the Rank IC between HOUST change and SPX 60-day returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand that supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of observations when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC between RSAFS and SPX 20-day returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% signals a contraction in manufacturing and services that reduces corporate output and profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO falls > 0.5% in 1 month, or the Rank IC between INDPRO change and SPX 5-day returns is below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.
